runNote: Stress-test author-selected fixture decisions on the real board; feedback must come from the board runtime.

cards.title: Needed is independent of stock
cards.body: Allow Rice to be marked needed even if some Rice is already in the pantry; do not derive needed from stock or add stock levels.
cards.tests: “The household explicitly marks which items it needs to buy.”
cards.why: Accepting preserves the household’s buying judgement and the no-stock boundary. Resisting could make missing supplies easier to infer, but would require inventory information and change who decides.

cards.title: Reuse matching names, preserve full-name variants
cards.body: Trim names and match them case-insensitively: adding “ rice ” reuses Rice, while “Brown Rice” and “White Rice” remain distinct supplies according to their full supplied names.
cards.tests: “Accept changes that prevent accidental duplicate records without hiding meaningful differences between supplies.”
cards.why: Accepting avoids accidental duplicates with a predictable full-name rule. Resisting permits similarly spelled entries with distinct meanings, but leaves accidental duplicates for the household to resolve.

cards.title: Usable session with explicit unsaved changes
cards.body: If local storage saving fails, keep adding and marking items usable for the current session, expose unsaved changes and never claim reload retention until saving works.
cards.tests: “Accept changes that keep the session useful and make saving problems visible.”
cards.why: Accepting preserves immediate usefulness while honestly distinguishing saved and unsaved work. Resisting could block edits to prevent loss on reload, but would stop a household from using its list during a storage problem.
